sourceEvidence.label: Canonical deployment design and delivery-boundary sources

assessment.summary: A temporary forced-command ingress is a design candidate, not an implementation or production authorization.

nonNegotiables: The full-Sigstore owner, lock-postverification, offline-closure, and explicit Risk A resume holds remain active.
The existing Japan runtime-config repair channel cannot be reused or widened.
No credentials, host state, workflow source, or production action is authorized by this addendum.
assumptions: The redacted production inventory must be refreshed before any execution Gate.
The payload can remain within a 64 MiB aggregate cap and a 24-hour retention window.

opportunities.title: Constrain a future Actions-to-host artifact delivery edge
opportunities.summary: Define a dedicated, forced-command receiver for a matched control-plane source and dependency artifact pair without changing the existing production control plane.
opportunities.diagnosis: Current artifact workflows and repository read access do not provide a bounded artifact-receiving authority, while the only existing production SSH workflow is deliberately purpose-specific.

evidence.claim: A new Risk A topology addendum is required for a proposed extra predecessor or delivery authority.
The dry run creates a review packet but has no production-host execution path.
The existing Japan SSH workflow is fixed-purpose and restrictive.
A distinct artifact receiver is required rather than widening repository read access or the repair identity.

desiredInvariants: Only the exact four-object, source-bound payload can reach the receiver.
The receiver provides no arbitrary command execution or network forwarding.
Every accepted object is digest-bound, size-bounded, owner-checked, and expires automatically.
Receiving a valid artifact never activates it, changes a release pointer, or restarts a service.

options.title: Retain no artifact ingress
options.summary: Keep the current no-host-delivery state and rely only on existing read-only repository access.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It preserves the existing repair-channel purpose boundary.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new receiver or credential exists.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Reconfirm no new delivery identity or workflow exists.

tradeoffs.assessment: There is no new data path.
There is no receiver process or buffer.
It cannot provide a controlled artifact delivery route.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm the downstream deployment program remains stopped.
Read back existing identity and workflow scope.

residualRisks: The approved deployment program remains unable to deliver Actions artifacts to the host.

options.title: Temporary forced-command artifact ingress
options.summary: Use a future dedicated low-privilege receiver with a protected Environment private key, a host-only public key, fixed object labels, digest checks, 64 MiB aggregate cap, and 24-hour expiry.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A new controlled edge can consume the dry-run artifact only after separate approval; the dry-run workflow itself remains non-executing.
The new identity avoids expanding the fixed-purpose repair channel.

tradeoffs.assessment: A forced command and fixed manifest constrain delivery, but the protected private key and receiver become new sensitive controls.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Negative protocol, manifest, size, expiry, command, TTY, forwarding, and digest tests must all fail closed.

tradeoffs.assessment: The path adds one bounded stream and hashing pass.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure 64 MiB transfer wall time against a defined target after implementation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Streaming and capped buffers should bound memory, but this remains unmeasured.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak receiver RSS for the maximum payload.

tradeoffs.assessment: Atomic receipt publication and no-replace behavior prevent partial payloads from becoming candidates.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject interrupted streams, duplicate deliveries, and expiry races.

tradeoffs.assessment: It introduces a protected Environment, a short-lived receiver, retention cleanup, and receipt review.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise creation, readback, expiry cleanup, key removal, and evidence-only receipt review.

tradeoffs.assessment: It requires a new deployment path but must not change the current pointer-based activation path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use disposable validation with synthetic artifacts and prove no release pointer or service change.

residualRisks: A correctly bounded ingress still cannot satisfy the separate owner, closure, or production-promotion gates.
Key exposure, receiver bugs, or retention failure remain fail-closed Gate conditions.

affectedComponents: Future dedicated workflow, receiver, and non-executable receipt schema only after separate approval.
workPackages: Create a bounded receiver and contract tests.
Create a protected manual workflow and exact-secret readback.
migrationNotes: Keep the existing release pointer and repair channel unchanged.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remove the protected secret and host public key under a separate approved destructive cleanup gate; preserve only aggregate-safe evidence.

opportunities.recommendation: Record temporary bounded ingress only as a later execution-Gate candidate; retain no ingress until all independent prerequisites are green.

openQuestions: Can the future selected full-Sigstore owner and offline closure gates become green without altering this delivery boundary?
Which protected GitHub Environment name and independent reviewers can be read back under a separate Settings Gate?
Can a disposable environment prove the exact receiver semantics without production data or activation?
